official.tuition_coverage_note: Successful PhD iRTP applicants receive 'a tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years'.
benefits: Tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years (PhD iRTP applicants)
Living allowance stipend for up to three years, $40,900 per annum (2027 rate)
Travel concession applied to the local transport OPAL card (PhD applicants)
Automatic consideration for the University-funded iMQRES in the same round
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand, and not an Australian permanent resident, at the time of application
Intend to reside in Sydney, Australia during candidature
Plan to undertake a Master of Research or Doctor of Philosophy in Session 1 2027 full-time
Have completed your degree; applicants in the final semester of their program are not eligible (except Macquarie applicants, and all PhD applicants applying through MQBS)
Hold a valid visa enabling the commencement of onshore study in Session 1 2027
Have confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher (compulsory for FOA, FMHHS and FSE; desirable for MQBS)
requirements: Select 'International Research Scholarship' as the scholarship type in the Macquarie graduate research application

Applicants already enrolled (commenced an MQ graduate research program in Session 2 2026 only) or holding a Macquarie PhD letter of offer from the last six months must submit the online graduate research Scholarship Only application instead
Meet the English language requirement for a Macquarie research degree and satisfy all admission criteria
Lodge a complete application before the deadline; incomplete applications are withdrawn and cannot be held over to a future round
documents: Confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher
Evidence of English language proficiency (approved test less than two years old, taken in a secure testing centre)
Full documentation of achievements to support assessment of qualifications
For a research masters or equivalent: thesis abstract, examiner reports, thesis copy, length, grade, examination process and the percentage of the research component
Evidence of published research, refereed conference presentations and substantial work-related research experience, where claimed
selection_criteria: Relevant research output and experience and/or potential
Alignment of the applicant's project with the University's Research Strategy and research priorities
Quality of the supervisory team and international standing of the research area (Research Environment considerations)
Overseas qualifications assessed using Australian Government guidelines for comparability to the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF)
coverage: Tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years
Living allowance stipend of $40,900 per annum for up to three years
Travel concession on the local transport OPAL card (PhD applicants)
application_method: Submit a Macquarie graduate research application selecting 'International Research Scholarship' as the scholarship type
Already enrolled or holding a recent PhD letter of offer: submit the online graduate research Scholarship Only application
Macquarie encourages applicants to submit as early as possible prior to the deadline
official.application_route: Apply directly to Macquarie University through the graduate research application selecting 'International Research Scholarship' (current students and recent offer-holders use the Scholarship Only route).
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand and not an Australian permanent resident at the time of application, and intend to reside in Sydney during candidature.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open across Macquarie's research areas: arts and social sciences, business, education, engineering, information technologies, language and linguistics, law, media, communications and creative arts, medicine and health, psychological sciences, science, and security, intelligence and criminology.
official.research_requirement: Confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher is compulsory for FOA, FMHHS and FSE applicants and desirable for MQBS; MRes and PhD applicants must meet the admission criteria for the respective degree.
official.duration: Up to three years for PhD applicants (tuition fee offset and stipend); MRes applicants may be counter-offered entry with a provisional three-year PhD
official.description: The International Research Training Program (iRTP) is the Australian Government's Research Training Program scholarship scheme for international graduate research students, administered by individual universities on behalf of the Department of Education. Macquarie administers it alongside the University-funded iMQRES, with a single application placing applicants in both schemes.
official.program_type: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) international scholarship administered by Macquarie University
official.english_requirement: Competent English for most Graduate Research courses: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (TOEFL iBT 86 on the old scale, PTE Academic 60). Proficient English applies to Macquarie Law School and English Literature research courses: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with no band below 6.5. Test scores must be less than two years old at application and online/home test versions are not accepted.

applicant_utility.summary: This round has already closed: the Session 1 2027 window ran 15 June to 31 July 2026, so new applicants should watch Macquarie's scholarship search page for the next international round and use the interval to lock in a supervisor and a valid English test. The package pairs a full tuition offset with a $40,900 per annum living allowance for up to three years plus an OPAL travel concession for PhD candidates, and every iRTP applicant is automatically considered for the University-funded iMQRES in the same round. Because the number of government RTP places shifts each year, that automatic iMQRES consideration is a genuine second chance rather than a formality.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International researchers with a completed degree, an aligned Macquarie supervisor and strong published output who can commit to full-time candidature in Sydney.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure written confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie researcher before applying; it is compulsory for FOA, FMHHS and FSE candidates
Book an approved English test early; scores must be under two years old and from a secure testing centre, and online or home versions are rejected
Assemble the full achievement file (thesis abstract, examiner reports, publications, conference papers) because overseas qualifications are compared to the AQF
Shape the research proposal around Macquarie's Research Strategy priorities and name how the supervisory team fits them
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete applications are withdrawn outright and cannot be held over to a future round
Applying while still in the final semester of your current degree; only Macquarie applicants (and all MQBS PhD applicants) are exempt
Receiving another equivalent or major award, or having already completed a research degree at the same or higher level
Failing to select 'International Research Scholarship' as the scholarship type, or using the wrong route instead of the Scholarship Only form
Missing supervisor confirmation for FOA, FMHHS or FSE, or lacking a valid visa for onshore commencement in Session 1 2027
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Overseas Student Health Cover, student visa charges and flights to Sydney are not listed among the iRTP benefits, and the $40,900 per annum stipend is fixed, so any gap between it and actual Sydney living costs (including supporting family) sits with the award-holder.
document_audit: Overseas qualifications are assessed against the AQF, so official transcripts and degree documents are essential; informal records will not establish comparability
English evidence older than two years, or from an online or home test sitting, does not meet the policy
Research output claims need the thesis detail Macquarie asks for: abstract, examiner reports, length, grade, examination process and research percentage
If you are mid-candidature or hold a recent offer, the standard application route will not capture you; the Scholarship Only form is mandatory
alerts: The 31 July 2026 11pm deadline has passed and nothing can be held over, so set an alert on the scholarship search page for the next round
If no outcome notification arrives by 15 November 2026, treat the application as unsuccessful rather than waiting
Industry or external top-ups are permitted only up to 100% of the stipend value; confirm before accepting outside funding
Award-holders already receiving a full scholarship or salary for the proposed program are excluded, even if the offer arrives later
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Lodge the Macquarie graduate research application with 'International Research Scholarship' selected and track the outcome by email; current students and recent offer-holders use the separate Scholarship Only online form.

The round page text says the application opened 6 July 2026, the portal listing shows an open date of 15 July 2026, and the FAQ publishes the standing Term 1 window as 1 August to 30 October. Standing windows for later rounds: Term 2, 1 December to 26 February; Term 3, 1 April to 18 June.
official.status_note: UNSW's scholarship portal lists the PUCA1029 Term 1 2027 round as Open, closing 30 October 2026; late applications and late supporting documentation are not accepted.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Offer 1 is 'a full tuition fee scholarship paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of program'; Offer 2 is '$20,000 per annum paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of program'.

Offer 2: $20,000 per annum paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of the program
Recipients could also receive guaranteed entry to the UNSW Professional Development Program

UEEC holders must be enrolled in the UNSW Institute of Languages and successfully complete the program before commencing in Term 1 2027
UAC International applicants and applicants with pending Year 12 (or equivalent) results may still apply by the deadline, but offers are made only to recipients with an unconditional Letter of Offer
requirements: Register an account (or log in) in the Scholarship Application Online portal and submit the PUCA1029 application
Answer all selection-criterion questions and provide evidence supporting each claim; unanswered questions or claims without supporting documentation will not be assessed

Extra-curricular activities such as sporting, cultural activities, volunteer or work experience
Reasons for undertaking studies at UNSW
UNSW reserves the right not to award a scholarship where there is no applicant of sufficient merit or eligibility and selection criteria are not met

No living-cost, travel or relocation support is published for PUCA1025
application_method: Find the PUCA1029 advertisement on the UNSW Scholarships website and register a scholarship account (as a future student if you have no offer yet)
Complete the PUCA1029 application, answering every selection-criterion question with evidence
Combine all supporting documents into a single English-language PDF under 10MB and upload before the deadline
official.application_route: Apply online through the Scholarship Application Online portal via the PUCA1029 round application, after or while awaiting a UNSW offer for Term 1 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: International students only; the PUCA1029 round is for commencing international students.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students; domestic applicants are not eligible for PUCA1025.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any UNSW undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree program, excluding UNSW Online and UNSW Canberra.
official.description: The International Scientia Coursework Scholarship (PUCA1025) is UNSW Sydney's flagship coursework scholarship for commencing international students, offered through the UNSW Scholarships for International Students round (PUCA1029), and pays either full tuition fees or $20,000 per annum towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of the program.

English language test scores for admission; the scholarship pages publish the UEEC route rather than IELTS/TOEFL score requirements

verification.notes: Award values, eligibility, selection criteria, deadlines and document rules were taken from the official PUCA1029 Term 1 2027 round page, the PUCA1029 FAQ and Supporting Documentation Guide PDFs on the UNSW Scholarships site, and UNSW's international scholarships page; the previous scholarships.online.unsw.edu.au detail URL now returns 404 and the portal has moved to scholarships.unsw.edu.au.

applicant_utility.summary: PUCA1025 is claimed through the single PUCA1029 round application, so one submission puts you in front of every international coursework scholarship in that round, including the full-tuition Offer 1. You must already hold, or be relying on a qualifying conditional offer for, a Term 1 2027 place by 30 October 2026, and every claim in the application needs documentary evidence inside one combined PDF. The award covers tuition only, so budget for Sydney living costs separately, and remember a full-tuition Offer 1 cannot be stacked with the International Student Award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international school leavers and postgraduate coursework applicants holding an unconditional UNSW offer for Term 1 2027 who can document leadership and sustained extra-curricular involvement.
application_readiness_checklist: Lodge the UNSW admission application first and push for the unconditional offer before 30 October 2026; eligibility hinges on holding it
Build the evidence file as you go, mapping each document (transcripts, certificates, reference letters, payslips) to a specific application question
Merge everything into one English PDF under 10MB and confirm the file opens cleanly after compression
Answer the 'why UNSW' question with specific, evidenced reasons rather than generic motivation
Email scholarships@unsw.edu.au with any questions at least a week before the deadline; later enquiries may not receive a reply
common_rejection_risks: Claims with no supporting document attached are not assessed at all, however strong the claim
Supporting documents that are not in English, were not professionally translated, or are more than three years old
Waiting for the scholarship outcome before applying to UNSW; the offer must be held by the deadline
Uploading several files or a file over 10MB; the portal accepts one combined file per applicant
Submitting after the AEST 11:59PM 30 October 2026 closing time; no late applications or late documents are accepted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition: accommodation, living costs, transport, Overseas Student Health Cover and visa fees, plus any tuition balance above the award. UNSW itself advises international students not to rely on scholarships alone, as no scholarship covers the full cost of studying and living in Australia.
document_audit: One file per applicant, so merge PDFs locally and verify readability after compressing to under 10MB
All documents must be in English; UNSW will not translate them and untranslated items are ignored in assessment
Evidence older than three years does not count, so refresh reference letters and certificates before applying
Conditional offers with outstanding Genuine Student or English language conditions do not qualify; only UEEC packages do
If final results are still pending, apply by the deadline anyway and flag your situation to the scholarships office by email
alerts: Offer 1 (full tuition) cannot be held together with the International Student Award, and only one international scholarship may be held at a time
The scholarship offer letter carries a lapse date; accept it before it expires or the award lapses
UNSW Scholarships charges no application or processing fee; any request for payment is a scam and should be reported to scholarships@unsw.edu.au
If your admission offer expires before the outcome, the Scholarships Office can liaise with Admissions to reinstate it, subject to course spot availability
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the Scholarship Application Online portal, submit the PUCA1029 application with the combined evidence PDF, then monitor the portal for statuses (being assessed, shortlisted, successful conditional offer, unsuccessful) and accept the offer letter before its lapse date.
